records.category: unsecured lending and unrecovered public funds
records.people: Hassan Basajjabalaba (businessman, owner of Haba Group of Companies); Bank of Uganda officials (not named in the source); Muwada Nkunyingi (chairperson, Committee on Commissions, Statutory Authorities and State Enterprises)
records.summary: Parliament's COSASE committee, questioning Bank of Uganda officials for a second time over queries raised in the Auditor General's report for financial year 2024/2025, found that the central bank had advanced Shs140 billion to Hassan Basajjabalaba's Haba Group of Companies without security and that not a shilling had been recovered since 2017; the committee resolved on 14 September 2026 to summon Basajjabalaba himself, and its chairperson said the outstanding amount had affected the operations of the central bank. This is a separate episode from the Auditor General's 2018 special audit of the seven closed banks already on the map: different borrower, different years, different committee sitting.
records.detail: The report is a Nile Post account of the committee sitting, carried by AllAfrica on 14 September 2026. It states the loan amount (Shs140 billion), the borrower (Haba Group of Companies), the absence of security, the nine years without repayment, and that Bank of Uganda officials were before the committee over Auditor General queries for FY 2024/2025. The article does not set out the Auditor General's detailed findings and does not carry Basajjabalaba's response, so the status is recorded as an open inquiry rather than a finding against any named person.
records.source_title: Uganda: Cosase Summons Hassan Basajjabalaba Over Shs140bn Bank of Uganda Loan (Nile Post, via AllAfrica)

records.people: Mubarak Nansamba (acting assistant commissioner, Treasury Services, Ministry of Finance); Tony Yawe (senior IT officer); Mark Kasiiku (data centre consultant); Leona Faith Kwikiriza and Eriphaz Sebiyonga (senior systems analysts); Bank of Uganda officials and Michael Atingi-Ego (deputy governor, who gave evidence)
records.summary: The Auditor General's forensic and IT audit, requested by the CID director on 24 October 2024 and tabled in Parliament on 9 January 2025, found that payment instructions worth 21,013,562.31 US dollars for the International Development Association and the African Development Fund had been altered before the files reached the Bank of Uganda, which then processed and externalised them; the audit concluded the alteration was made at the Accountant General's Office and recorded weak controls at both the Ministry of Finance and the Bank of Uganda, with no red flag raised on either payment. The bank is therefore both the channel of the loss and the subject of a control finding, and the primary perpetration is located outside it.
records.detail: Two payments were diverted: 6,134,137.75 dollars meant for IDA, redirected to a Tokyo company on 10 September 2024 and processed by the Bank of Uganda on 12 September, which has not been recovered; and 8,596,824.26 dollars meant for the African Development Fund, redirected to MJS International, London, on 26 September 2024 and externalised by the bank two days later, of which Citibank New York confirmed a reversal of 8,205,103.81 dollars on 14 November 2024. A third attempt, 6,674,320.75 dollars due on 15 January 2025, was stopped by a SWIFT mismatch. Finance Ministry officials including the Accountant General were arrested and prosecuted. Yawe and Kasiiku denied involvement. The deputy governor told COSASE on 17 December 2024 that the transactions stemmed from an erroneous Ministry of Finance directive.
records.source_title: $21m BoU fraud report reveal shocking details (The Observer, Uganda)

blanks.note: Office of the Auditor General of Seychelles, 'Activity Report and Audited Accounts of OAG for 2024' (7.5 MB PDF on nationalassembly.sc, 96,558 characters of extracted text, downloaded and grepped in full). The inversion test comes out positive on membership and negative on findings: para 1.2 and para 2.24 state the Auditor General is mandated to audit the Central Bank of Seychelles plus 7 public enterprises and 76 other statutory bodies, and Appendix 'Category 5' confirms he is the statutory auditor of the Central Bank; para 3.10 shows the Central Bank audit is among the ten outsourced to contracted firms. The report records no irregularity, qualification, adverse opinion or finding against the Central Bank anywhere (grepped for qualifi/adverse opinion/irregular/fraud/misappropriat/disclaim; every hit is boilerplate or about other bodies). The only certification exception named is PMC, whose accounts were not ready. The vein is open but a level down: the CBS audit certificates themselves, and the two 2024 special audit reviews listed on page 6, were not opened.

blanks.note: Auditor General of Zambia, report on the accounts of the Republic for the year ended 31 December 2019 (the 'Final AG's Report' PDF hosted by News Diggers, 1.42 MB, 36,660 characters extracted, grepped in full). 'Bank of Zambia' appears three times: once in the acronym list, and once as the section heading 'Delayed Transfer of Revenue to Bank of Zambia', read in full. That finding is against commercial banks and the Ministry of Finance under a January 2018 service level agreement: K12,905,956 of revenue transferred one to two days late, penalties of K1,290,596 unpaid at 31 August 2020. The Bank of Zambia is only the destination account, not the subject, and the finding is too remote even for counterparty_only. Separately NOT reached: the National Assembly's 'Report of the Committee on Parastatal Bodies on the Report of the Auditor General for the financial year ended 31st December 2023', which would be the per-entity route — parliament.gov.zm returned HTTP 000 to curl on every attempt and three retries, and WebFetch rejected the URL with 'url exceeds the maximum fetchable length'. That host is NOT in the round's curl-friendly list and should be treated as unreachable from here.

blanks.label: refused
blanks.note: Lusaka Times, 12 July 2012, 'BoZ employee arrested money laundering' (https://www.lusakatimes.com/2012/07/12/boz-employee-arrested-money-laundering). A real second episode in shape — Micheal Mulembe, a Monitoring and Control Officer, with Melinda Mulembe and Chris Salanda Zulu, charged with fraudulent false accounting, theft by servant and money laundering over K150,337,856.60 and K76,445,978.22 credited out of the bank's trading profit and loss account between 1 January 2011 and 5 July 2012, arrested by the Drug Enforcement Commission. Refused because the article body never names the institution: it says only 'a named bank'. The Bank of Zambia attribution rests on the headline and URL slug alone, and the map's existing ZMB record is a 2015 DEC arrest of a BoZ employee for money laundering, so the risk of filing a different-year duplicate on a slug is real. Worth one fetch of a second outlet next round; if any source names the Bank of Zambia in its text, this converts.

blanks.label: refused
blanks.note: The audit of the National Bank of Ethiopia by MSE Audit Service LLP for the year beginning July 2022, carried out under the IMF programme, approved late March 2025 and published on the NBE site on 4 April 2025, as reported in detail by The Reporter (Ethiopia), 'NBE audit reveals scale of forex losses, mounting government debt' (https://www.thereporterethiopia.com/44561/), read in full. Every finding is financial, not misconduct: negative general reserve of close to one billion birr after losses of 1.8 billion (2022) and 1.4 billion birr; net forex losses above 12 billion birr; direct advances to government of 130 billion birr and interest-bearing bonds of 430 billion at 30 June 2023; 137 billion birr extended to state-owned banks; and a 1 billion dollar Saudi time deposit from 2015 for which 'the NBE did not offer any form of collateral'. The report states no irregularity, mismanagement or misappropriation, so nothing here is a corruption case. This is the auditor's report the next round would otherwise spend a fetch on. The audited financial statements themselves on nbe.gov.et were not opened.

notes: Budget and host behaviour: about 23 fetches. parliament.gov.zm is unreachable — HTTP 000 to curl on two different document paths with three retries each, and its URLs are long enough that WebFetch refuses them outright with 'url exceeds the maximum fetchable length'. That cost four calls and killed the per-entity Zambian parliamentary route for this round. diggers.news and nationalassembly.sc both serve large PDFs to plain curl without complaint.
closed_negatives.json: the cases_unavailable map contains none of the 29 assigned countries, so nothing here re-reads a document an earlier round closed.

party_names.json was grepped before any institution name was written. The map already carries 'Office of the Auditor General (Uganda)', 'Office of the Auditor General (Zambia)', 'Auditor General of Seychelles, audit review carried out by Grant Thornton Audit and Accounting Limited Abu Dhabi' and 'Mauritius Investment Corporation'; no new party spelling is introduced by either record filed.

The quote field is omitted from both records on purpose. Everything quotable here came to me through an extraction tool rather than from text I copied off the page, and brief_common.md says to leave the field out in exactly that case. The verbatim strings the extraction reported, if a later round wants to verify them against the page: Nkunyingi, 'Since 2017, not a single shilling has been recovered.'; and the Auditor General, 'This confirms that the change in payment details was made at the Accountant General's Office.'

The doubtful call in this file is counterparty_only on the second Uganda record. The Auditor General located the alteration of the payment files at the Accountant General's Office, which makes the Ministry of Finance the primary subject, but the same audit recorded weak controls at the Bank of Uganda, which processed and externalised both payments with no red flag raised. I set counterparty_only false because the bank is named in a control finding of its own rather than appearing merely as the ministry's counterparty, and wrote that split into the summary so a reviewer can see the judgement and reverse it to true without re-reading the source. Uganda is already coloured on this row, so nothing turns on it visually.
